newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Coceral gloomy on EU wheat export prospects.
newsitem.headline: Coceral gloomy on EU wheat export prospects.

text.p: Limited import demand and increased competition from Canada and Australia will make wheat export prospects difficult for the rest of 1996/97, according to Coceral, the EU grain trade lobby.
"The international situation for soft wheat in grains is not looking good," Coceral said in minutes received on Monday of a meeting of the EU cereals advisory committee on February 7.
Coceral said there was only small potential for sales to Algeria, Morocco and and Iraq.
It added that Canada is expected to reduce prices with the reopening of the lakes after the winter freeze.
Coceral warned that from April and May part of import demand will be shifted towards the U.S. new crop where the price objective is $130.
It urged the European Commission to adopt a more dynamic export policy by adjusting prices downwards from current levels of around $145 a tonne so as to exploit potential markets.

"Up until now (the) Trade has made an effort in covering its needs, but the Commission must be more aggressive," it said, adding that it was preferable to export on the free market rather than put the grain into intervention stores.
